prompt: Let $R$ already be a non-strict partial order on $A$. Which extra condition is necessary and sufficient for it to be a total (linear) order? All variables range over $A$.

answers.explanation: Every pair of distinct elements must be comparable. Reflexivity already handles equal elements.
Symmetry would reduce a partial order to equality, which is not total on a set of size at least two.
This contradicts reflexivity on a nonempty domain.
Transitivity already holds and does not force comparability.
Reflexivity already makes the relation serial, even when some distinct elements are incomparable.
Antisymmetry already holds in a partial order.
Reflexivity already holds in a partial order.
This requires both directions between distinct elements and conflicts with antisymmetry.
Together with reflexivity this permits only equality, not general total orders.
A greatest element need not make all other elements comparable.
